**2B.8 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Best-supported reading: Srettha’s 2024 security posture was reactive and containment-oriented, centered on the Myanmar border. I found no credible evidence that he used military spending or mobilization to intimidate neighbors, reward security elites, or project personal strength. The public record instead shows border coordination, humanitarian assistance, and ASEAN-managed de-escalation.

|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Deputy Foreign Minister and National Security delegation visit Mae Sot to receive the latest update on the Thailand-Myanmar border situation](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/dpmfm-dpmim-dm-nscsg-maesot-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 23, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/dpmfm-dpmim-dm-nscsg-maesot-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand sent a high-level civilian-security delegation including foreign affairs, defense, armed forces, police, and NSC officials to coordinate support for local agencies at the border. This is evidence of mobilization for a real border-security need, not for intimidation or patronage. | `2B.8`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Summary of Weekly Press Briefing 19 April 2024 at 11.00 hrs.](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/weeklypressbriefing190424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 19, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/weeklypressbriefing190424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand said it was monitoring the Myanmar situation closely, created a special committee, and remained open to dialogue with stakeholders. That is controlled crisis management, not a show of force for prestige. | `2B.8`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 18, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac | ASEAN called for immediate restraint, cessation of violence, and protection of civilians, and Thailand joined that line. That points to security policy aimed at containment and civilian protection, not at rewarding hardliners or projecting strength. | `2B.8`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Thailand working ‘relentlessly’ to solve Myanmar crisis - Srettha](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha) | Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News | May 24, 2024 | https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha | Srettha said Thailand was working to reduce spillover violence and end the Myanmar crisis. That is consistent with responding to genuine security needs rather than using mobilization for domestic or regional signaling. | `2B.8`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |

**Search gap**

- I found no public 2024 evidence of Thailand’s military budget being expanded for patronage, elite capture, or neighbor intimidation under Srettha.
- I also found no credible evidence of military mobilization used as a prestige project or as personal-power projection.
- The record is mostly border containment and humanitarian coordination, so the strongest conclusion is that his security posture was defensive and limited, not expansionary or self-serving.
